chunks: From him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, the Imam from whom the report is transmitted.
key_terms.عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, a narrator in the chain.
key_terms.عَنْهُ: From him; a connective transmission term referring to the previous narrator.
key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حُمْرَانَ: Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān, a narrator in the chain.
key_terms.مِثْلَهُ: Its like; meaning the same as the preceding report in wording or meaning.

ai.seo_question: What does “مِثْلَهُ” mean in a hadith of Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām, and how is it used as a supporting narration?
ai.summary: This report gives a brief sanad/isnad ending with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, then states: “the like of it,” indicating that the wording or ruling is the same as a previous hadith. In context, it functions as a supporting transmission for the same legal teaching related to false accusation, insult, insinuation, explicit abuse, or false testimony.
